summary: A hand closes on a garment or holds an instrument to use it. In a siege or pursuit the verb describes capture.

senses.definition: Joseph’s garment is caught in his flight. Joshua’s men seize the king of Ai alive, and the same verb can describe taking a whole city.
The object identifies the skill. Jubal’s descendants play string and wind instruments, the sailor handles an oar, and the reaper grasps a sickle.
A king trying to escape will be taken captive. Psalm 10 speaks of being caught in schemes, with the identity of those caught supplied from the surrounding clause.

stems.gloss: catch or grasp with the hands

senses.gloss: catch or grasp with the hands
senses.definition: The proverb pictures a small lizard in a king’s palace. The verb can address someone able to catch it or describe the creature itself taking hold.

cognates.note: Hebrew left-dotted sin corresponds here to Aramaic samekh.

note: Proverbs 30:28 permits two readings of the person of the verb. Topheth in the valley of Hinnom and the burning place in Isaiah 30:33 have no demonstrated derivation from the verb of capture.
